newsitem.title: UK: IPE oil futures barely changed, trade slow.
newsitem.headline: IPE oil futures barely changed, trade slow.

text.p: IPE Brent crude and gas oil futures were barely changed on Thursday in low volume trade, with the market likely to hold within a tight range, brokers said.
By 0950 GMT September Brent was unchanged from Thursday's open at $18.39 a barrel, with gas oil 25 cents higher at $165.25 a tonne.

The market would be keeping an eye out for any move higher by U.S crude during the London afternoon. NYMEX September crude is tipped by some to make an upside break towards the psychological $20.00 a barrel mark.
NYMEX crude futures trading on Access were last done at $19.68 a barrel, five cents higher from the NYMEX settle at $19.63.
"If Brent can clear $18.50, $18.70/80 will be next," GNI Research said in a report. "But we are constantly wary of a potential breakdown if resistance levels remain in place."
News of the timing of the resumption of Iraq's oil-sale deal remained on the back-burner.
Iraq needs to sell 1.5 million barrels of crude per day in order to raise the $1 billion it needs to buy humanitarian aid before the deal ends in September.
The second phase of the deal started on June 8.
